title: A Reactor is a library, not a service: it stores and syncs documents while a host application like Switchboard exposes the API
content:
A **Reactor** is the Powerhouse library (`@powerhousedao/reactor`) that applies reducers, orders operations into a deterministic log, and routes them to processors and sync channels. It is *not* a service: it has no `main()` and it does not open a port. A **host application** embeds it and supplies storage, network, UI surfaces, and the package registry. When you run `ph vetra --watch`, a local host application starts and embeds a Reactor for you. Reactors provide:

- Document storage and hosting
- Document synchronization across clients
- Conflict resolution
- Operation history verification (by rerunning operations)

Reactors can be configured for:
- Local storage (development/Studio Mode)
- Centralized cloud storage
- Decentralized storage networks

The Reactor has no public API of its own — that surface belongs to the host. **Switchboard**, the API host that wraps a Reactor, is what exposes the GraphQL subgraphs: system, analytics, and per-model subgraphs such as document-editor, vetra-package, subgraph-module, processor-module and app-module, plus vetra-read-model. Switchboard also provides the WebSocket server for subscriptions and the MCP server for AI agent integration.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: The Reactor is a library handling document storage, conflict resolution, and operation verification. Host applications such as Switchboard expose the GraphQL/MCP API.
